title: Spring Boot from First Principles
goal: Understand what Spring does behind the annotations.

topics.title: Build dependencies and auto-configuration

tasks.title: Explain the concept without notes
Complete the guided exercise
Verify the independent exercise

topics.description: Spring Boot supplies dependency management and conditional configuration for common application needs.
learningGoals: The application builds outside the IDE
Dependencies and automatic defaults can be explained
examples: A web dependency brings MVC infrastructure.

material.explanation: Spring Boot supplies dependency management and conditional configuration for common application needs. Inspect what is actually configured instead of assuming an annotation performs every required action. Choose one supported stack and let its dependency management keep related libraries aligned.

workedExample.scenario: A web dependency brings MVC infrastructure.
steps: Inspect configured beans and conditions.
Remove a dependency and explain the behavior change.

commonMistakes: A starter does not implement your business rules or make every configuration correct.
material.independentExercise: Explain which parts differ from the plain-Java project's startup.

acceptanceCriteria: The application builds outside the IDE
Dependencies and automatic defaults can be explained

topics.title: IoC
topics.description: Inversion of control moves selected decisions, such as construction or invocation, to a framework.
learningGoals: Manual and managed construction are understood
Domain code does not require the container
examples: Manual startup constructs repository then service.

tasks.title: Explain the idea in your own words
Work through a concrete example
Check a boundary or failure case

material.explanation: Inversion of control moves selected decisions, such as construction or invocation, to a framework. Explain the manual equivalent first so the container's work is visible. Domain behavior can remain ordinary Java regardless of who creates the objects.

workedExample.scenario: Manual startup constructs repository then service.
steps: A container can perform that wiring.
The service still enforces the same use-case rules.

commonMistakes: IoC does not mean business logic must depend on Spring APIs.
material.independentExercise: Trace who creates and calls each part of a coupon request.
recallQuestions: Which control moved to the framework?

acceptanceCriteria: Manual and managed construction are understood
Domain code does not require the container

topics.title: Dependency Injection
topics.description: Dependency injection supplies collaborators from outside an object rather than hiding their construction inside it.
learningGoals: Required dependencies are explicit
Policy tests run without Spring startup
examples: Construct RefreshTokenService with a repository, generator, and hasher.

tasks.title: Explain Dependency Injection in your own words
Work through the example and predict the result
Check a boundary or failure case without AI implementation help

material.explanation: Dependency injection supplies collaborators from outside an object rather than hiding their construction inside it. Constructor injection makes required dependencies visible and supports ordinary unit tests. The container is one wiring mechanism, not the definition of DI itself.

workedExample.scenario: Construct RefreshTokenService with a repository, generator, and hasher.
steps: Substitute fakes in a test.
Use real adapters in application configuration.

commonMistakes: Dependency injection can exist without any annotations.
guidedExercise: Run its tests without a Spring context
material.independentExercise: Move a hard-coded clock out of a service constructor body.

acceptanceCriteria: Required dependencies are explicit
Policy tests run without Spring startup

topics.title: Bean
topics.description: A bean is an object managed by the Spring container.
learningGoals: Bean scope is explained accurately
Request-specific mutable state is not shared
examples: Several requests use one singleton service.

tasks.title: Explain the idea in your own words
Work through a concrete example
Check a boundary or failure case

material.explanation: A bean is an object managed by the Spring container. Know its scope and initialization boundaries. A singleton scope describes one managed instance per relevant container, not universal thread safety or an application-wide distributed singleton.

workedExample.scenario: Several requests use one singleton service.
steps: Its immutable dependencies are shared safely.
A mutable request-specific field would mix users.

commonMistakes: A singleton bean is not automatically thread-safe.
material.independentExercise: Design a stateless coupon service with request data kept in method variables.
recallQuestions: Which state should not live in that bean?

acceptanceCriteria: Bean scope is explained accurately
Request-specific mutable state is not shared

topics.title: ApplicationContext
topics.description: ApplicationContext manages configured objects and their dependencies.
learningGoals: Startup failures are traced to configuration
Business dependencies remain explicit
examples: A service requires a TokenHasher.

tasks.title: Explain the idea in your own words
Work through a concrete example
Check a boundary or failure case

material.explanation: ApplicationContext manages configured objects and their dependencies. Resolve objects at the application composition boundary rather than passing the context into domain logic as a service locator. Understand startup failures as dependency or configuration failures.

workedExample.scenario: A service requires a TokenHasher.
steps: The context resolves one matching bean.
Missing or ambiguous candidates produce a startup problem.

commonMistakes: Calling getBean throughout domain code hides dependencies.
material.independentExercise: Wire two hasher implementations deliberately without ambiguous resolution.
recallQuestions: Why avoid service-location in domain methods?

acceptanceCriteria: Startup failures are traced to configuration
Business dependencies remain explicit

topics.title: Component Scanning
topics.description: Component scanning discovers eligible classes within configured package boundaries.
learningGoals: Scan boundaries are documented
Component discovery can be explained
examples: A controller is outside the scanned package tree.

tasks.title: Explain the idea in your own words
Work through a concrete example
Check a boundary or failure case

material.explanation: Component scanning discovers eligible classes within configured package boundaries. It does not discover every class on the machine. Keep scanning intentional and understand why moving a component can change application startup.

workedExample.scenario: A controller is outside the scanned package tree.
steps: It is not registered by that scan.
Adjust package placement or explicit configuration.

commonMistakes: Adding a stereotype does not guarantee a bean is discovered.
guidedExercise: Move a small component and observe registration
material.independentExercise: Organize coupon packages so infrastructure is discoverable without broad accidental scanning.

acceptanceCriteria: Scan boundaries are documented
Component discovery can be explained

topics.title: @Configuration
topics.description: Configuration classes describe how collaborators are assembled.
learningGoals: Wiring and business rules remain separate
Environment-specific collaborators are explicit
examples: Configuration supplies Clock and TokenHasher.

tasks.title: Explain the idea in your own words
Work through a concrete example
Check a boundary or failure case

material.explanation: Configuration classes describe how collaborators are assembled. Keep environment-specific choices there while keeping business decisions in domain behavior. Understand proxied versus non-proxied configuration when directly invoking factory methods.

workedExample.scenario: Configuration supplies Clock and TokenHasher.
steps: The service receives those beans.
Tests can supply controlled alternatives.

commonMistakes: Configuration methods are not a place for request-level business logic.
material.independentExercise: Compose a token use case without adding annotations to its domain types.

acceptanceCriteria: Wiring and business rules remain separate
Environment-specific collaborators are explicit

topics.title: @Bean
topics.description: A Bean factory method registers its returned object with the container.
learningGoals: The intended product is registered
Manual and managed instances are not confused
examples: A factory receives a repository and clock.

tasks.title: Explain the idea in your own words
Work through a concrete example
Check a boundary or failure case

material.explanation: A Bean factory method registers its returned object with the container. Method parameters can express dependencies resolved by Spring. Use factories for types you do not annotate or for deliberate construction decisions.

workedExample.scenario: A factory receives a repository and clock.
steps: It constructs a plain Java service.
The resulting service becomes a managed bean.

commonMistakes: Calling an arbitrary new operation does not register the result as a bean.
material.independentExercise: Register a third-party component through an explicit factory.

acceptanceCriteria: The intended product is registered
Manual and managed instances are not confused

topics.title: External configuration and secrets

tasks.title: Explain the concept without notes
Complete the guided exercise
Verify the independent exercise

topics.description: External configuration supplies deployment-specific values without hard-coding them into business logic.
learningGoals: Invalid required settings fail early
Real secrets remain outside source and diagnostics
examples: A token lifetime comes from validated configuration.

material.explanation: External configuration supplies deployment-specific values without hard-coding them into business logic. Bind related settings, validate required values early, and distinguish secrets from ordinary settings. Avoid logging resolved credentials or committing real secret files.

workedExample.scenario: A token lifetime comes from validated configuration.
steps: Reject a nonpositive value at startup.
Inject the resulting duration into the use case.

commonMistakes: Moving a password to a tracked properties file is not secret management.
material.independentExercise: Configure database connection details without exposing them in source or logs.

acceptanceCriteria: Invalid required settings fail early
Real secrets remain outside source and diagnostics

topics.title: Proxy
topics.description: A proxy wraps a target to apply behavior such as transactions or advice.
learningGoals: The advised call path is traced
Bypass cases are understood and tested
examples: An external caller invokes a transactional service.

tasks.title: Explain Proxy in your own words
Work through the example and predict the result
Check a boundary or failure case without AI implementation help

material.explanation: A proxy wraps a target to apply behavior such as transactions or advice. A call must pass through the relevant proxy to receive that behavior. Direct self-invocation on the target may bypass the wrapper and change semantics.

workedExample.scenario: An external caller invokes a transactional service.
steps: The proxy begins the transaction.
A self-call to another advised method may not create the expected boundary.

commonMistakes: An annotation alone does not prove every call passes through a proxy.
material.independentExercise: Explain one transaction bug caused by manual construction or self-calls.
recallQuestions: Which object receives the call first?

acceptanceCriteria: The advised call path is traced
Bypass cases are understood and tested

topics.title: AOP
topics.description: AOP applies selected behavior around defined invocation points.
learningGoals: Advice behavior is explainable for failure too
Domain rules remain visible in ordinary code
examples: Advice measures service execution time.

tasks.title: Explain the idea in your own words
Work through a concrete example
Check a boundary or failure case

material.explanation: AOP applies selected behavior around defined invocation points. It is useful for genuinely cross-cutting concerns but can hide control flow. Keep business rules explicit and understand ordering when multiple interceptors affect the same call.

workedExample.scenario: Advice measures service execution time.
steps: It records duration on success and failure.
It does not decide coupon eligibility.

commonMistakes: AOP is not a reason to hide core domain rules in annotations.
guidedExercise: Trace before, target, and after behavior
material.independentExercise: Explain the limits of timing a proxied method with an external dependency.
recallQuestions: What control flow does advice add?

acceptanceCriteria: Advice behavior is explainable for failure too
Domain rules remain visible in ordinary code

topics.title: @Transactional
topics.description: Transactional advice defines a database unit of work around a managed call.
learningGoals: Partial database changes roll back on specified failures
The real proxy and database path is tested
examples: A use case revokes X and inserts Y.

tasks.title: Explain @Transactional in your own words
Work through the example and predict the result
Check a boundary or failure case without AI implementation help

material.explanation: Transactional advice defines a database unit of work around a managed call. Understand which failures cause rollback, which connection participates, and which calls reach the proxy. Keep external calls out of unnecessarily long lock-holding transactions.

workedExample.scenario: A use case revokes X and inserts Y.
steps: An insertion failure follows the configured rollback policy.
An integration test verifies X remains unrevoked.

commonMistakes: Unit-testing a manually constructed service does not prove transaction advice works.
material.independentExercise: Compare a working boundary with a self-invocation mistake.
recallQuestions: Which exceptions trigger rollback under your policy?
What does this transaction not cover?

acceptanceCriteria: Partial database changes roll back on specified failures
The real proxy and database path is tested

topics.title: Spring MVC
topics.description: Spring MVC routes requests, binds inputs, and invokes handlers.
learningGoals: Transport concerns stay in the controller
The service remains independently testable
examples: POST redeems a coupon code from the path.

tasks.title: Explain the idea in your own words
Work through a concrete example
Check a boundary or failure case

material.explanation: Spring MVC routes requests, binds inputs, and invokes handlers. Keep the controller focused on transport concerns and delegate the use case. Follow a request from routing through validation to response rather than treating annotations as magic.

workedExample.scenario: POST redeems a coupon code from the path.
steps: Bind the request and identify the caller.
Invoke the application service and translate its result.

commonMistakes: A controller should not own persistence and all domain rules.
material.independentExercise: Implement one coupon endpoint against an already-tested service.
recallQuestions: Which rules belong below the controller?

acceptanceCriteria: Transport concerns stay in the controller
The service remains independently testable

topics.title: Validation
topics.description: Validate input shape and simple transport constraints before domain work.
learningGoals: Invalid requests never reach unsafe domain work
Direct domain calls preserve invariants
examples: A redemption request contains a negative amount.

tasks.title: Explain the idea in your own words
Work through a concrete example
Check a boundary or failure case

material.explanation: Validate input shape and simple transport constraints before domain work. Domain invariants still apply to calls from other entry points. Use a consistent error contract for invalid requests without serializing internal exceptions.

workedExample.scenario: A redemption request contains a negative amount.
steps: Reject invalid transport input.
The domain also rejects invalid amounts if called directly.

commonMistakes: DTO annotations are not the only place a business invariant should exist.
guidedExercise: Test invalid JSON and invalid fields
material.independentExercise: Separate syntactic email checks from registration uniqueness and credential policy.
recallQuestions: What must the domain enforce independently?

acceptanceCriteria: Invalid requests never reach unsafe domain work
Direct domain calls preserve invariants

topics.title: Exception Handling
topics.description: Translate known failures into consistent transport responses at the boundary.
learningGoals: Failure categories have stable public codes
Internal traces and secrets do not reach clients
examples: Coupon redemption reports exhausted usage.

tasks.title: Explain the idea in your own words
Work through a concrete example
Check a boundary or failure case

material.explanation: Translate known failures into consistent transport responses at the boundary. Keep domain errors independent of HTTP and avoid exposing exception messages that may contain credentials or database details. Preserve full safe diagnostics internally for unexpected failures.

workedExample.scenario: Coupon redemption reports exhausted usage.
steps: Map it to the documented business error.
A database outage uses a different safe failure response.

commonMistakes: Returning a stack trace to the client is not useful error handling.
guidedExercise: Test one expected and unexpected failure
material.independentExercise: Implement a consistent coupon error representation.
recallQuestions: Which failure is expected business behavior?

acceptanceCriteria: Failure categories have stable public codes
Internal traces and secrets do not reach clients

topics.title: Spring Data
topics.description: Spring Data can generate repository behavior from contracts and queries.
learningGoals: Query behavior matches the intended contract
Concurrency-sensitive updates are verified
examples: A session query returns entities and related users.

tasks.title: Explain the idea in your own words
Work through a concrete example
Check a boundary or failure case

material.explanation: Spring Data can generate repository behavior from contracts and queries. Understand the actual SQL and transaction semantics rather than assuming generated methods preserve a multi-step invariant. Keep domain behavior independent from persistence implementation choices.

workedExample.scenario: A session query returns entities and related users.
steps: Inspect generated SQL and access patterns.
Avoid accidental extra queries while mapping the response.

commonMistakes: Generated repositories do not make every compound update atomic.
guidedExercise: Compare a JDBC query with its repository equivalent
material.independentExercise: Implement a conditional token claim and verify affected-row semantics.
recallQuestions: Which use-case guarantee still needs explicit design?

acceptanceCriteria: Query behavior matches the intended contract
Concurrency-sensitive updates are verified

topics.title: Persistence mapping and query costs

tasks.title: Explain the concept without notes
Complete the guided exercise
Verify the independent exercise

topics.description: Persistence mapping connects Java values to stored rows.
learningGoals: The list endpoint has a measured query budget
No unplanned lazy access escapes its boundary
examples: List ten sessions and their owners.

material.explanation: Persistence mapping connects Java values to stored rows. Understand identity, relationships, fetching, and transaction-dependent access. Response DTOs should not accidentally trigger unbounded lazy loads or expose the persistence graph.

workedExample.scenario: List ten sessions and their owners.
steps: Inspect whether each owner triggers another query.
Choose a query or projection matching the response.

commonMistakes: Object navigation can perform database work that is invisible in the Java expression.
guidedExercise: Count queries for a list endpoint
Map results inside a defined boundary
material.independentExercise: Eliminate an N+1 response without loading unrelated relationships.
recallQuestions: When can a getter cause I/O?
What data does the response actually need?

acceptanceCriteria: The list endpoint has a measured query budget
No unplanned lazy access escapes its boundary

topics.title: Spring Security
topics.description: Spring Security integrates credential processing and authorization into request handling.
learningGoals: Protected endpoints reject missing or invalid identity
Authenticated cross-user operations are denied
examples: A protected request reaches authentication filters.

tasks.title: Explain the idea in your own words
Work through a concrete example
Check a boundary or failure case

material.explanation: Spring Security integrates credential processing and authorization into request handling. Trace its filter chain and failure paths, then connect them to your session policy. Keep security decisions explicit; framework defaults may not match your API or cookie flow.

workedExample.scenario: A protected request reaches authentication filters.
steps: A principal is established or the request is rejected.
Resource ownership is checked before mutation.

commonMistakes: A successful authentication filter does not enforce all domain ownership rules.
guidedExercise: Trace login and a protected request
Distinguish authentication failure from access denial
material.independentExercise: Implement session ownership checks and test a cross-user request.

acceptanceCriteria: Protected endpoints reject missing or invalid identity
Authenticated cross-user operations are denied

topics.title: Test layers and integration checks

tasks.title: Explain the concept without notes
Complete the guided exercise
Verify the independent exercise

topics.description: Use the smallest test layer that proves the behavior.
learningGoals: Each important boundary has an appropriate check
Small policy tests avoid framework startup
examples: A coupon rule is tested directly.

material.explanation: Use the smallest test layer that proves the behavior. Plain unit tests check policy; web tests check binding and response mapping; database and full application tests check integration boundaries. Avoid loading the entire context for every small rule.

workedExample.scenario: A coupon rule is tested directly.
steps: A handler test checks invalid input mapping.
A real database test verifies rollback and uniqueness.

commonMistakes: A mocked repository cannot prove constraints, locks, or actual SQL.
guidedExercise: Classify three existing tests by what they prove
material.independentExercise: Build a test matrix for token rotation with unit, HTTP, and database cases.
recallQuestions: What does this test actually exercise?

acceptanceCriteria: Each important boundary has an appropriate check
Small policy tests avoid framework startup

exercises.title: Framework Boundary Tests

tasks.title: Verify: The matrix covers transport, policy, and persistence guarantees
Verify: The real transaction path is exercised
Verify: Every test identifies what it proves and what remains outside scope

exercises.description: Prove the behavior that annotations and mocks cannot establish alone.
learningGoals: Prove the behavior that annotations and mocks cannot establish alone.
Demonstrate the acceptance criteria with observable evidence.
examples: A failure occurs after the first database write.
requirements: Test malformed request binding and validation
Verify exception translation and protected endpoint rules
Run a real-database rollback test through the managed service
Demonstrate a self-invocation or manual-construction transaction bypass
Inspect one generated query path for unwanted database work
constraints: Use small unit or slice tests where sufficient
Use full integration only for the boundary being verified
deliverables: Working solution or design, as specified
Evidence matrix: behavior, test layer, dependency

material.explanation: Choose tests according to the guarantee you need. Mock-based HTTP tests can validate response mapping, but transaction and SQL behavior need a real integration path. Keep the matrix small enough that the purpose of every test is clear.

workedExample.scenario: A failure occurs after the first database write.
steps: Calling the managed service rolls back both writes under its policy.
A bypassed proxy path reveals why annotation presence alone is insufficient.

commonMistakes: Do not treat a successful demonstration as proof of all rules. Explain rejection behavior and show state after failure.
guidedExercise: Name one guarantee for each test layer.
Compare a proxied and bypassed call.
material.independentExercise: Find a test that loads unnecessary framework infrastructure and reduce it without losing the proven behavior.
recallQuestions: Which call actually reaches the transaction proxy?

acceptanceCriteria: The matrix covers transport, policy, and persistence guarantees
The real transaction path is exercised
Every test identifies what it proves and what remains outside scope
